question: Now that the sampler is GPU-bound, is 2-way output-column parallelism across two B70s worth building?
method: offline, exclusive GPUs, synthetic LTX-shaped blocks, everything graph-captured per device exactly as the landed packet does
findings: Two B70s replay their graphs FULLY concurrently: running both costs the same as either alone (factor 1.999). Cross-device concurrency is real and needs no special scheduling.
Cross-device gathers are cheap: 0.0399 ms per activation pair, so even six per block across 48 blocks is 11.5 ms per step.

But halving the weights does NOT halve the time: 737.5 MB takes 104.31 ms and 368.8 MB takes 66.43 ms, a 1.57x ratio, not 2x. Small projections do not scale: an earlier probe measured ff.net.0.proj at 1.977x for a half-width split but attn.to_q at only 1.256x.
Fitting time = a + b*bytes gives a fixed floor of about 28.5 ms per 48-block chain that does not shrink with the split: duplicated elementwise and normalisation work plus small-GEMM inefficiency.
four_way_note: A 4-way split is not placeable: a quarter transformer is 10.5 GB per card, but XPU2 holds the 25 GB text encoder, so 35.5 GB would be needed there. A 3-way split over XPU0/1/3 fits (about 14 GB each, XPU3 also holding 2.7 GB of VAEs) and extrapolates to roughly 1.6x.
decision: Real but bounded: about 1.41x on the GPU portion of the sampler for a large re-sharding build with its own exactness re-qualification. Recorded and deferred behind the cheaper removal of the remaining per-call Python.
limitations: synthetic blocks with the checkpoint shapes, not the real checkpoint code or weights
the split model is an idealisation: it omits the norm/gather placement rules a real implementation must respect
audio_ff N-splits were previously found NOT bit-identical at 256 tokens, so a real build cannot split every layer
no exactness claim is made for any split here; only timing
